tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## claude.ai Buildkite
This is the Buildkite MCP Server. It provides access to the Buildkite CI/CD API, enabling you to manage and inspect pipelines, builds, jobs, logs, clusters, tests, artifacts, and annotations.

Start here: Before using most tools, call user_token_organization to retrieve the organization slug. Nearly every other tool requires the org_slug parameter, and this call is the fastest way to discover it.

Skill discovery: Always call list_skills early in a session — it's cheap (names and one-line descriptions only) and surfaces guidance not visible in any tool's name or schema. When a task matches a listed skill (e.g. debugging a build failure, tuning search_logs), call load_skill for that guide — it covers parameter tuning, caching behavior, and details beyond the summaries below.

Authorization: Tools available depend on the scopes and organization access granted to the configured API token. A 401 response means the token is invalid, expired, or revoked and requires reauthentication. A 403 response means the credentials were accepted but access was denied, commonly because the token lacks a required scope or organization access, or the user lacks permission.

Common pitfalls:

build_number is a sequential integer string (e.g. "42"), not a UUID. Build, job, artifact, and log tools all require this identifier — do not use the build's UUID id field.

Build failure investigation: start with get_build_failure_summary. It combines build state, blocking failed and canceled jobs, promised failures from running jobs, soft-failed jobs (listed after blocking failures and canceled jobs), bounded log tails, relevant annotations, and failed tests in one response; jobs that never ran (broken, waiting_failed, blocked_failed, unblocked_failed) fill the remaining max_jobs slots unless include_never_ran_jobs is false. Use the individual build, job, log, annotation, and test tools only when the summary identifies an area that needs deeper inspection.

Pipeline authoring: always check pipeline YAML with validate_pipeline before creating or updating a pipeline, or before committing changes to .buildkite/pipeline.yml. It validates against the official pipeline schema locally — the call itself never contacts the Buildkite API and works regardless of the configured token's scopes — and catches structural errors that would otherwise fail silently at upload time. A valid result does not guarantee runtime correctness (environment variable interpolation, plugin configuration, dynamically generated steps).

Build comparison: use compare_builds when asked what changed since a build worked, or to compare two builds. Without an explicit baseline it selects an earlier successful build on the same pipeline and branch. Report the selected baseline and unmatched steps; shared failing steps do not establish a shared cause or justify a retry. Timings cover final attempts, not total retry cost or build wall-clock duration.

Job state "broken" means the pipeline configuration decided, when the job was created, that it would not run: an `if` condition or `branches` filter did not match, `parallelism` was 0, or the step was marked `skip`. Broken is never caused by another job failing, never fails a build, and is normal in passing builds. Jobs stopped by a failed dependency are `waiting_failed`, `blocked_failed` or `unblocked_failed` instead; those appear only in builds that actually failed and are consequences of an upstream failure, not root causes. None of these four states ran, so they have no logs. `failed` = ran and exited non-zero; `skipped` = an external factor (e.g. a newer build superseded it). To explain a red build, investigate only `failed`, `timed_out`, `expired` jobs that are not `soft_failed`, as well as `running` jobs that have non-zero `promised_exit_status`.

Soft failures: a job with `soft_failed` true actually ran and exited unsuccessfully, but the step's `soft_fail` setting allowed that exit status, so the failure did not block the build. `soft_fail` may allow every non-zero exit or only listed `exit_status` values, so the same step can still fail … [truncated]

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Buildkite
This is the Buildkite MCP Server. It provides access to the Buildkite CI/CD API, enabling you to manage and inspect pipelines, builds, jobs, logs, clusters, tests, artifacts, and annotations.

Start here: Before using most tools, call user_token_organization to retrieve the organization slug. Nearly every other tool requires the org_slug parameter, and this call is the fastest way to discover it.

Skill discovery: Always call list_skills early in a session — it's cheap (names and one-line descriptions only) and surfaces guidance not visible in any tool's name or schema. When a task matches a listed skill (e.g. debugging a build failure, tuning search_logs), call load_skill for that guide — it covers parameter tuning, caching behavior, and details beyond the summaries below.

Authorization: Tools available depend on the scopes and organization access granted to the configured API token. A 401 response means the token is invalid, expired, or revoked and requires reauthentication. A 403 response means the credentials were accepted but access was denied, commonly because the token lacks a required scope or organization access, or the user lacks permission.

Common pitfalls:

build_number is a sequential integer string (e.g. "42"), not a UUID. Build, job, artifact, and log tools all require this identifier — do not use the build's UUID id field.

Build failure investigation: start with get_build_failure_summary. It combines build state, blocking failed and canceled jobs, promised failures from running jobs, soft-failed jobs (listed after blocking failures and canceled jobs), bounded log tails, relevant annotations, and failed tests in one response; jobs that never ran (broken, waiting_failed, blocked_failed, unblocked_failed) fill the remaining max_jobs slots unless include_never_ran_jobs is false. Use the individual build, job, log, annotation, and test tools only when the summary identifies an area that needs deeper inspection.

Pipeline authoring: always check pipeline YAML with validate_pipeline before creating or updating a pipeline, or before committing changes to .buildkite/pipeline.yml. It validates against the official pipeline schema locally — the call itself never contacts the Buildkite API and works regardless of the configured token's scopes — and catches structural errors that would otherwise fail silently at upload time. A valid result does not guarantee runtime correctness (environment variable interpolation, plugin configuration, dynamically generated steps).

Build comparison: use compare_builds when asked what changed since a build worked, or to compare two builds. Without an explicit baseline it selects an earlier successful build on the same pipeline and branch. Report the selected baseline and unmatched steps; shared failing steps do not establish a shared cause or justify a retry. Timings cover final attempts, not total retry cost or build wall-clock duration.

Job state "broken" means the pipeline configuration decided, when the job was created, that it would not run: an `if` condition or `branches` filter did not match, `parallelism` was 0, or the step was marked `skip`. Broken is never caused by another job failing, never fails a build, and is normal in passing builds. Jobs stopped by a failed dependency are `waiting_failed`, `blocked_failed` or `unblocked_failed` instead; those appear only in builds that actually failed and are consequences of an upstream failure, not root causes. None of these four states ran, so they have no logs. `failed` = ran and exited non-zero; `skipped` = an external factor (e.g. a newer build superseded it). To explain a red build, investigate only `failed`, `timed_out`, `expired` jobs that are not `soft_failed`, as well as `running` jobs that have non-zero `promised_exit_status`.

Soft failures: a job with `soft_failed` true actually ran and exited unsuccessfully, but the step's `soft_fail` setting allowed that exit status, so the failure did not block the build. `soft_fail` may allow every non-zero exit or only listed `exit_status` values, so the same step can still fail … [truncated]

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index ae9db7a0..7ca8f793 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
 ### Added
 
 - **`RefScope.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes` shrinks the haves of a relay fetch.** A relay fetch offers the source every target tip as a have. For refs that each carry their own history, such as one orphan history per session checkpoint, those tips cannot shorten the pack, and a repository with thousands of them sent thousands of have lines for a run that changed one branch. Under the named prefixes, a target ref is now offered only when the run updates it, as its own old value. Replicate and sync's incremental relay honor it. Sync's closure fetch for fast-forward checks and bootstrap still offer every tip. Which refs are synced or pruned does not change. Entries are literal prefixes of target ref names and must start with `refs/`; end a namespace with a slash. Naming refs that do share history keeps the copy complete but resends objects the target already holds, and the larger pack can hit a pack or request size limit.
+- **Relay fetches drop target tips that another target tip already implies, when the target supports it.** Most target tips are ancestors of other tips, yet each one was sent to the source as a have. When the target advertises the `entire-maximal` ls-refs feature (entiredb), git-sync now lists the target's mirrored namespaces over upload-pack v2, at most once per run and only when the run fetches a pack. The listing uses its own connection, so a `FollowInfoRefsRedirect` redirect on upload-pack discovery never moves the push. The target marks each ref that no other listed ref reaches. Refs the target did not mark are left out of the haves for sync's closure fetch, sync's incremental relay, and replicate. Refs outside the listed namespaces, and refs under `IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes`, stay for the existing have rules to handle. If a marked ref has moved since the listing, for example because this run pushed it, that fetch offers every tip. entiredb accepts the argument before it advertises it, so `SyncPolicy.AssumeTargetMaximal` (CLI `--assume-target-maximal`) sends it without the advertisement. Use it only against an entiredb target whose every node accepts the argument. A target that does not advertise the feature and is not assumed to support it, `--protocol v1`, an SSH target, a failed listing, or one that breaks the target's own marking rules keeps the old behavior. Bootstrap is unchanged. Fewer haves never drop an object from the pack. If the source lacks a marked commit, the fetch resends history the target already holds.
 
 ### Changed
 
@@ -19,6 +20,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- **Credentials from the git credential helper no longer follow an `/info/refs` redirect to an unrelated host.** With `FollowInfoRefsRedirect`, a connection that authenticated through the helper and was then redirected to another site sent that helper's credentials with its later requests to the new host. Helper credentials are now held to the site they were looked up for, the same rule explicit tokens already followed. A host that challenges for credentials gets the helper's answer for that host instead.
 - **A branch whose new tip the target already holds under another ref now fast-forwards instead of failing the sync.** The planning fetch names every target ref as a have, so the source prunes such a tip from the pack and the ancestry check aborted the run with `load source commit …: object not found`. A mirror of NixOS/nixpkgs hit this whenever `nixos-unstable` advanced to a commit `master` had already delivered. A check the pruned store cannot settle is now resolved with one tree:0 commit-graph fetch of that tip against the ref's own target hash: a real fast-forward updates, and a rewind blocks as `not an ancestor`. A source that cannot serve that fetch (protocol v1, no filter support) leaves the ref blocked with the reason instead of crashing. Builds on [#79](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/79).
 - **`BootstrapLogger` now receives the bootstrap planning and progress lines.** They went only to the `-v` stderr log, so an embedder saw the GitHub size lookup and then nothing until the first checkpoint upload. A bootstrap that stalled while planning logged the size preflight and then nothing until its timeout. Every planning line now also goes to `BootstrapLogger`, with the logger's own attributes and the caller's context. Phase and checkpoint progress goes at Info: planning checkpoints, fetching the commit graph, planned remaining branches with their counts, push attempting, group pushed, branch finalized. A push the target refused or timed out, and resume markers left on the target, go at Warn; a push git-sync stops itself at its byte budget and then splits stays at Info, so a successful bootstrap logs no warnings. Lines logged once per branch (subsumed by trunk, already on target) go at Debug, so a repository with thousands of branches does not emit thousands of Info records per attempt. Error text from the target is sanitized. `-v` shows every line it showed before. ([#134](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/134))
 - **Batched bootstrap of a repository with thousands of branches now makes progress.** It used to fetch the commit graph of every branch, one request per branch, before it pushed anything. On a branch-heavy repository that planning alone outlasted a 30-minute sync budget, so each attempt timed out with nothing on the target and started again (ENT-3617). The trunk is now planned and pushed first, so an attempt that times out still leaves it on the target. The remaining branches share one commit-graph fetch. Small branches are pushed in shared packs that create their refs directly, so a fetch and a push deliver many of them. A group whose pack is over budget splits in half. A branch too big to share a pack, or one with a resume marker, keeps its own checkpointed batch as before. `FetchCommitParents` now takes the wants as a list of hashes.

+++ b/internal/gitproto/maximal.go
@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+package gitproto
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/transport"
+)
+
+// MaximalFeature is entiredb's ls-refs extension. It is the capability
+// feature, the request argument, and the ref attribute. A server that
+// receives it marks each listed ref whose commit no other listed ref reaches.
+// It leaves a ref unmarked only when it has proved that another listed ref's
+// commit reaches it, so the marked refs imply the history of every listed ref.
+const MaximalFeature = "entire-maximal"
+
+// ErrMaximalUnsupported reports that a server does not advertise
+// MaximalFeature over protocol v2.
+var ErrMaximalUnsupported = errors.New("server does not advertise " + MaximalFeature)
+
+// ErrMaximalInconsistent reports a MaximalFeature listing that breaks the
+// server's own rules: a ref listed twice, two refs at the same object marked
+// differently, or a non-empty listing with no mark at all. Every non-empty set
+// of refs has a maximal one, so a listing like that cannot be trusted to drop
+// any have.
+var ErrMaximalInconsistent = errors.New("inconsistent " + MaximalFeature + " listing")
+
+// MaximalTips is a target's ls-refs listing with the MaximalFeature marks.
+// Reduce uses it to drop redundant haves.
+type MaximalTips struct {
+	marked   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
+	unmarked map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
+}
+
+// Marked and Unmarked report the listing's size, for logs and tests.
+func (m *MaximalTips) Marked() int   { return len(m.marked) }
+func (m *MaximalTips) Unmarked() int { return len(m.unmarked) }
+
+// ListMaximalTips lists conn's upload-pack refs under prefixes with the
+// MaximalFeature marks. It returns ErrMaximalUnsupported, before sending
+// ls-refs, when the server does not speak protocol v2 or, unless
+// assumeSupported is set, does not advertise the feature. Protocol v2 forbids
+// an argument the server did not advertise, so set assumeSupported only for a
+// server known to accept it; one that does not fails the ls-refs request.
+//
+// List only refs the source also holds. The source ignores a have it lacks,
+// and a marked tip it lacks hides the unmarked refs behind it, so the fetch
+// carries history the target already has. That costs bytes, never
+// correctness.
+func ListMaximalTips(ctx context.Context, conn Conn, prefixes []string, assumeSupported bool) (*MaximalTips, error) {
+	data, err := RequestInfoRefs(ctx, conn, transport.UploadPackService, GitProtocolV2)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	caps, err := DecodeV2Capabilities(bytes.NewReader(data))
+	if err != nil {
+		// A v1 advertisement: the server did not negotiate v2.
+		return nil, ErrMaximalUnsupported
+	}
+	if !caps.Supports("ls-refs") || (!assumeSupported && !caps.LSRefsSupports(MaximalFeature)) {
+		return nil, ErrMaximalUnsupported
+	}
+	args := []string{MaximalFeature}
+	for _, prefix := range prefixes {
+		args = append(args, "ref-prefix "+prefix)
+	}
+	body, err := EncodeCommand("ls-refs", caps.RequestCapabilities(), args)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	resp, err := PostRPC(ctx, conn, transport.UploadPackService, body, true, "upload-pack ls-refs "+MaximalFeature)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return decodeMaximalLSRefs(bytes.NewReader(resp))
+}
+
+func decodeMaximalLSRefs(r *bytes.Reader) (*MaximalTips, error) {
+	m := &MaximalTips{
+		marked:   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
+		unmarked: map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
+	}
+	// The server marks by peeled object, so every ref at one object carries
+	// the same mark.
+	markOf := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
+	reader := NewPacketReader(r)
+	for {
+		kind, payload, err := reader.ReadPacket()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		if kind == PacketFlush {
+			if len(m.unmarked) > 0 && len(m.marked) == 0 {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d refs, none marked", ErrMaximalInconsistent, len(m.unmarked))
+			}
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		if kind != PacketData {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected packet type %v in ls-refs response", kind)
+		}
+		fields := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(string(payload)))
+		if len(fields) < 2 {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs response line %q", payload)
+		}
+		name := plumbing.ReferenceName(fields[1])
+		// HEAD is not a have: the branch it names carries the same mark.
+		if fields[0] == "unborn" || name == plumbing.HEAD {
+			continue
+		}
+		if !plumbing.IsHash(fields[0]) {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs object id %q", fields[0])
+		}
+		hash := plumbing.NewHash(fields[0])
+		identity := hash
+		marked := false
+		for _, attr := range fields[2:] {
+			if attr == MaximalFeature {
+				marked = true
+			} else if peeled, ok := strings.CutPrefix(attr, "peeled:"); ok && plumbing.IsHash(peeled) {
+				identity = plumbing.NewHash(peeled)
+			}
+		}
+		if _, dup := m.marked[name]; dup {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
+		}
+		if _, dup := m.unmarked[name]; dup {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
+		}
+		if prev, ok := markOf[identity]; ok && prev != marked {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: refs at %s marked differently", ErrMaximalInconsistent, identity)
+		}
+		markOf[identity] = marked
+		if marked {
+			m.marked[name] = hash
+		} else {
+			m.unmarked[name] = hash
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// Reduce returns haves without the refs the listing proved redundant. A nil
+// receiver returns haves unchanged. keep, when non-nil, names refs Reduce must
+// never drop, for a caller that filters those refs by rules of its own.
+//
+// An unmarked ref is implied only through a marked ref that reaches it, and
+// the listing does not say which one. So Reduce drops anything only when every
+// marked ref is in haves at its listed hash. A ref that moved since the
+// listing, such as one this run pushed, keeps the whole map unreduced. An
+// unmarked ref is dropped only at its listed hash. Refs the listing did not
+// cover stay.
+func (m *MaximalTips) Reduce(
+	haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
+	keep func(plumbing.ReferenceName) bool,
+) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
+	// No marks proves nothing; decodeMaximalLSRefs already rejects that
+	// listing, and this keeps a hand-built one from dropping every have.
+	if m == nil || len(m.unmarked) == 0 || len(m.marked) == 0 {
+		return haves
+	}
+	for name, hash := range m.marked {
+		if got, ok := haves[name]; !ok || got != hash {
+			return haves
+		}
+	}
+	out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash, len(haves))
+	for name, hash := range haves {
+		if listed, ok := m.unmarked[name]; ok && listed == hash && (keep == nil || !keep(name)) {
+			continue
+		}
+		out[name] = hash
+	}
+	return out
+}

+// targetRefs without the refs the target proved redundant (see

+//
+// The reduction comes first because it needs every marked ref in the map. It
+// leaves independent-history refs to FetchHaves: an updated one may be
+// unmarked behind an unchanged one, and FetchHaves keeps the updated ref's old
+// value while dropping the unchanged one, so a reduction there would lose the
+// only have that shortens the update. A marked independent ref FetchHaves
+// drops reaches only its own namespace's history, so no other ref the
+// reduction drops depended on it.
+//
+// fetches says whether the caller will fetch a pack with these haves. The
+// listing costs round trips, so a run that fetches nothing (converged,
+// delete-only, or headed for a path that offers no haves) never asks for it.
+func (s *syncSession) fetchHaves(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
+	plans []planner.BranchPlan,
+	fetches bool,
+) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
+	if fetches && fetchesPack(plans) {
+		targetRefs = s.maximalTips(ctx).Reduce(targetRefs, s.independentHistoryRef)
+	}
+	return planner.FetchHaves(targetRefs, plans, s.cfg.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes)
+}
+
+func (s *syncSession) independentHistoryRef(name plumbing.ReferenceName) bool {
+	for _, prefix := range s.cfg.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes {
+		if prefix = strings.TrimSpace(prefix); prefix != "" && strings.HasPrefix(name.String(), prefix) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// fetchesPack reports whether plans need objects from the source: a delete
+// moves no objects.
+func fetchesPack(plans []planner.BranchPlan) bool {
+	for _, plan := range plans {
+		if plan.Action == planner.ActionCreate || plan.Action == planner.ActionUpdate {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// maximalTips asks the target, once per run, which of its refs no other ref
+// reaches (gitproto.MaximalFeature). Every target tip is a have by default,
+// and most tips are ancestors of others, so a large target sends far more
+// have lines than the fetch needs.
+//
+// It returns nil, and the caller keeps every tip, when the target does not
+// advertise the feature (unless Config.AssumeTargetMaximal is set), when
+// protocol v1 is pinned, when the target has too few refs to gain anything,
+// when the target is reached over SSH, or when the listing fails or breaks the
+// server's own rules. An SSH server whose sshd does not accept GIT_PROTOCOL
+// answers the v2 probe with its full v0 ref advertisement, which can be
+// megabytes for a ref list this run already holds. HTTP and remote helpers
+// answer v2 with a short capability list. The listing is an optimization, so a
+// failure is logged and not returned.
+//
+// The listing runs on its own connection, never the push connection. With
+// FollowInfoRefsRedirect, upload-pack discovery may redirect to a read host,
+// and on a shared HTTPConn that redirect would carry the push and its
+// credentials there too.
+//
+// The listing covers only the namespaces this run mirrors. A marked target ref
+// the source lacks would hide the refs behind it from the fetch. Mirrored refs
+// came from the source, while a target-only namespace may not have.
+func (s *syncSession) maximalTips(ctx context.Context) *gitproto.MaximalTips {
+	t := s.target
+	if t == nil || t.conn == nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+	if t.maximalListed {
+		return t.maximal
+	}
+	t.maximalListed = true
+	if s.cfg.ProtocolMode == protocolModeV1 || len(t.refMap) < 2 || isSSHEndpoint(t.conn) {
+		return nil
+	}
+	probe, err := newConn(s.cfg.Target, "target", s.stats, s.cfg.HTTPClient)
+	if err != nil {
+		if s.logger != nil {
+			s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips unavailable; offering every target tip as a have", slog.Any("error", err))
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	defer probe.Close()
+	probe.SetProgressWriter(t.conn.ProgressWriter())
+	tips, err := gitproto.ListMaximalTips(ctx, probe, maximalRefPrefixes(planConfig(s.cfg)), s.cfg.AssumeTargetMaximal)
+	if err != nil {
+		if s.logger != nil && !errors.Is(err, gitproto.ErrMaximalUnsupported) {
+			s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips unavailable; offering every target tip as a have", slog.Any("error", err))
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	if s.logger != nil {
+		s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips", slog.Int("marked", tips.Marked()), slog.Int("unmarked", tips.Unmarked()))
+	}
+	t.maximal = tips
+	return tips
+}
+
+// maximalRefPrefixes is the target-side scope of the maximal listing: the
+// include prefixes when set, otherwise the namespaces the source listing uses.
+// A mapping keeps its kind (branch or tag), so the same prefixes cover its
+// target name. A ref outside the scope is unlisted, and Reduce keeps it.
+func maximalRefPrefixes(cfg planner.PlanConfig) []string {
+	var include []string
+	for _, p := range cfg.IncludeRefPrefixes {
+		if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
+			include = append(include, p)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(include) > 0 {
+		return include
+	}
+	return planner.RefPrefixes(cfg)
+}
+
+func isSSHEndpoint(conn gitproto.Conn) bool {
+	ep := conn.Endpoint()
+	return ep != nil && (ep.Scheme == "ssh" || ep.Scheme == "git+ssh")
+}

5	@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
6	 ### Added
7	 
8	 - **`RefScope.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes` shrinks the haves of a relay fetch.** A relay fetch offers the source every target tip as a have. For refs that each carry their own history, such as one orphan history per session checkpoint, those tips cannot shorten the pack, and a repository with thousands of them sent thousands of have lines for a run that changed one branch. Under the named prefixes, a target ref is now offered only when the run updates it, as its own old value. Replicate and sync's incremental relay honor it. Sync's closure fetch for fast-forward checks and bootstrap still offer every tip. Which refs are synced or pruned does not change. Entries are literal prefixes of target ref names and must start with `refs/`; end a namespace with a slash. Naming refs that do share history keeps the copy complete but resends objects the target already holds, and the larger pack can hit a pack or request size limit.
9	+- **Relay fetches drop target tips that another target tip already implies, when the target supports it.** Most target tips are ancestors of other tips, yet each one was sent to the source as a have. When the target advertises the `entire-maximal` ls-refs feature (entiredb), git-sync now lists the target's mirrored namespaces over upload-pack v2, at most once per run and only when the run fetches a pack. The listing uses its own connection, so a `FollowInfoRefsRedirect` redirect on upload-pack discovery never moves the push. The target marks each ref that no other listed ref reaches. Refs the target did not mark are left out of the haves for sync's closure fetch, sync's incremental relay, and replicate. Refs outside the listed namespaces, and refs under `IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes`, stay for the existing have rules to handle. If a marked ref has moved since the listing, for example because this run pushed it, that fetch offers every tip. entiredb accepts the argument before it advertises it, so `SyncPolicy.AssumeTargetMaximal` (CLI `--assume-target-maximal`) sends it without the advertisement. Use it only against an entiredb target whose every node accepts the argument. A target that does not advertise the feature and is not assumed to support it, `--protocol v1`, an SSH target, a failed listing, or one that breaks the target's own marking rules keeps the old behavior. Bootstrap is unchanged. Fewer haves never drop an object from the pack. If the source lacks a marked commit, the fetch resends history the target already holds.
10	 
11	 ### Changed
12	 
13	@@ -19,6 +20,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
14	 
15	 ### Fixed
16	 
17	+- **Credentials from the git credential helper no longer follow an `/info/refs` redirect to an unrelated host.** With `FollowInfoRefsRedirect`, a connection that authenticated through the helper and was then redirected to another site sent that helper's credentials with its later requests to the new host. Helper credentials are now held to the site they were looked up for, the same rule explicit tokens already followed. A host that challenges for credentials gets the helper's answer for that host instead.
18	 - **A branch whose new tip the target already holds under another ref now fast-forwards instead of failing the sync.** The planning fetch names every target ref as a have, so the source prunes such a tip from the pack and the ancestry check aborted the run with `load source commit …: object not found`. A mirror of NixOS/nixpkgs hit this whenever `nixos-unstable` advanced to a commit `master` had already delivered. A check the pruned store cannot settle is now resolved with one tree:0 commit-graph fetch of that tip against the ref's own target hash: a real fast-forward updates, and a rewind blocks as `not an ancestor`. A source that cannot serve that fetch (protocol v1, no filter support) leaves the ref blocked with the reason instead of crashing. Builds on [#79](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/79).
19	 - **`BootstrapLogger` now receives the bootstrap planning and progress lines.** They went only to the `-v` stderr log, so an embedder saw the GitHub size lookup and then nothing until the first checkpoint upload. A bootstrap that stalled while planning logged the size preflight and then nothing until its timeout. Every planning line now also goes to `BootstrapLogger`, with the logger's own attributes and the caller's context. Phase and checkpoint progress goes at Info: planning checkpoints, fetching the commit graph, planned remaining branches with their counts, push attempting, group pushed, branch finalized. A push the target refused or timed out, and resume markers left on the target, go at Warn; a push git-sync stops itself at its byte budget and then splits stays at Info, so a successful bootstrap logs no warnings. Lines logged once per branch (subsumed by trunk, already on target) go at Debug, so a repository with thousands of branches does not emit thousands of Info records per attempt. Error text from the target is sanitized. `-v` shows every line it showed before. ([#134](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/134))
20	 - **Batched bootstrap of a repository with thousands of branches now makes progress.** It used to fetch the commit graph of every branch, one request per branch, before it pushed anything. On a branch-heavy repository that planning alone outlasted a 30-minute sync budget, so each attempt timed out with nothing on the target and started again (ENT-3617). The trunk is now planned and pushed first, so an attempt that times out still leaves it on the target. The remaining branches share one commit-graph fetch. Small branches are pushed in shared packs that create their refs directly, so a fetch and a push deliver many of them. A group whose pack is over budget splits in half. A branch too big to share a pack, or one with a resume marker, keeps its own checkpointed batch as before. `FetchCommitParents` now takes the wants as a list of hashes.

90	+// MaximalFeature is entiredb's ls-refs extension. It is the capability
91	+// feature, the request argument, and the ref attribute. A server that
92	+// receives it marks each listed ref whose commit no other listed ref reaches.
93	+// It leaves a ref unmarked only when it has proved that another listed ref's
94	+// commit reaches it, so the marked refs imply the history of every listed ref.

158	+func decodeMaximalLSRefs(r *bytes.Reader) (*MaximalTips, error) {
159	+	m := &MaximalTips{
160	+		marked:   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
161	+		unmarked: map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
162	+	}
163	+	// The server marks by peeled object, so every ref at one object carries
164	+	// the same mark.
165	+	markOf := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
166	+	reader := NewPacketReader(r)
167	+	for {
168	+		kind, payload, err := reader.ReadPacket()
169	+		if err != nil {
170	+			return nil, err
171	+		}
172	+		if kind == PacketFlush {
173	+			if len(m.unmarked) > 0 && len(m.marked) == 0 {
174	+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d refs, none marked", ErrMaximalInconsistent, len(m.unmarked))
175	+			}
176	+			return m, nil
177	+		}
178	+		if kind != PacketData {
179	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected packet type %v in ls-refs response", kind)
180	+		}
181	+		fields := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(string(payload)))
182	+		if len(fields) < 2 {
183	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs response line %q", payload)
184	+		}
185	+		name := plumbing.ReferenceName(fields[1])
186	+		// HEAD is not a have: the branch it names carries the same mark.
187	+		if fields[0] == "unborn" || name == plumbing.HEAD {
188	+			continue
189	+		}
190	+		if !plumbing.IsHash(fields[0]) {
191	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs object id %q", fields[0])
192	+		}
193	+		hash := plumbing.NewHash(fields[0])
194	+		identity := hash
195	+		marked := false
196	+		for _, attr := range fields[2:] {
197	+			if attr == MaximalFeature {
198	+				marked = true
199	+			} else if peeled, ok := strings.CutPrefix(attr, "peeled:"); ok && plumbing.IsHash(peeled) {
200	+				identity = plumbing.NewHash(peeled)
201	+			}
202	+		}
203	+		if _, dup := m.marked[name]; dup {
204	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
205	+		}
206	+		if _, dup := m.unmarked[name]; dup {
207	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
208	+		}
209	+		if prev, ok := markOf[identity]; ok && prev != marked {
210	+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: refs at %s marked differently", ErrMaximalInconsistent, identity)
211	+		}
212	+		markOf[identity] = marked
213	+		if marked {
214	+			m.marked[name] = hash
215	+		} else {
216	+			m.unmarked[name] = hash
217	+		}
218	+	}
219	+}

221	+// Reduce returns haves without the refs the listing proved redundant. A nil
222	+// receiver returns haves unchanged. keep, when non-nil, names refs Reduce must
223	+// never drop, for a caller that filters those refs by rules of its own.
224	+//
225	+// An unmarked ref is implied only through a marked ref that reaches it, and
226	+// the listing does not say which one. So Reduce drops anything only when every
227	+// marked ref is in haves at its listed hash. A ref that moved since the
228	+// listing, such as one this run pushed, keeps the whole map unreduced. An
229	+// unmarked ref is dropped only at its listed hash. Refs the listing did not
230	+// cover stay.
231	+func (m *MaximalTips) Reduce(
232	+	haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
233	+	keep func(plumbing.ReferenceName) bool,
234	+) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
235	+	// No marks proves nothing; decodeMaximalLSRefs already rejects that
236	+	// listing, and this keeps a hand-built one from dropping every have.
237	+	if m == nil || len(m.unmarked) == 0 || len(m.marked) == 0 {
238	+		return haves
239	+	}
240	+	for name, hash := range m.marked {
241	+		if got, ok := haves[name]; !ok || got != hash {
242	+			return haves
243	+		}
244	+	}
245	+	out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash, len(haves))
246	+	for name, hash := range haves {
247	+		if listed, ok := m.unmarked[name]; ok && listed == hash && (keep == nil || !keep(name)) {
248	+			continue
249	+		}
250	+		out[name] = hash
251	+	}
252	+	return out
253	+}

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index ae9db7a0..7ca8f793 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
 ### Added
 
 - **`RefScope.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes` shrinks the haves of a relay fetch.** A relay fetch offers the source every target tip as a have. For refs that each carry their own history, such as one orphan history per session checkpoint, those tips cannot shorten the pack, and a repository with thousands of them sent thousands of have lines for a run that changed one branch. Under the named prefixes, a target ref is now offered only when the run updates it, as its own old value. Replicate and sync's incremental relay honor it. Sync's closure fetch for fast-forward checks and bootstrap still offer every tip. Which refs are synced or pruned does not change. Entries are literal prefixes of target ref names and must start with `refs/`; end a namespace with a slash. Naming refs that do share history keeps the copy complete but resends objects the target already holds, and the larger pack can hit a pack or request size limit.
+- **Relay fetches drop target tips that another target tip already implies, when the target supports it.** Most target tips are ancestors of other tips, yet each one was sent to the source as a have. When the target advertises the `entire-maximal` ls-refs feature (entiredb), git-sync now lists the target's mirrored namespaces over upload-pack v2, at most once per run and only when the run fetches a pack. The listing uses its own connection, so a `FollowInfoRefsRedirect` redirect on upload-pack discovery never moves the push. The target marks each ref that no other listed ref reaches. Refs the target did not mark are left out of the haves for sync's closure fetch, sync's incremental relay, and replicate. Refs outside the listed namespaces, and refs under `IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes`, stay for the existing have rules to handle. If a marked ref has moved since the listing, for example because this run pushed it, that fetch offers every tip. entiredb accepts the argument before it advertises it, so `SyncPolicy.AssumeTargetMaximal` (CLI `--assume-target-maximal`) sends it without the advertisement. Use it only against an entiredb target whose every node accepts the argument. A target that does not advertise the feature and is not assumed to support it, `--protocol v1`, an SSH target, a failed listing, or one that breaks the target's own marking rules keeps the old behavior. Bootstrap is unchanged. Fewer haves never drop an object from the pack. If the source lacks a marked commit, the fetch resends history the target already holds.
 
 ### Changed
 
@@ -19,6 +20,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- **Credentials from the git credential helper no longer follow an `/info/refs` redirect to an unrelated host.** With `FollowInfoRefsRedirect`, a connection that authenticated through the helper and was then redirected to another site sent that helper's credentials with its later requests to the new host. Helper credentials are now held to the site they were looked up for, the same rule explicit tokens already followed. A host that challenges for credentials gets the helper's answer for that host instead.
 - **A branch whose new tip the target already holds under another ref now fast-forwards instead of failing the sync.** The planning fetch names every target ref as a have, so the source prunes such a tip from the pack and the ancestry check aborted the run with `load source commit …: object not found`. A mirror of NixOS/nixpkgs hit this whenever `nixos-unstable` advanced to a commit `master` had already delivered. A check the pruned store cannot settle is now resolved with one tree:0 commit-graph fetch of that tip against the ref's own target hash: a real fast-forward updates, and a rewind blocks as `not an ancestor`. A source that cannot serve that fetch (protocol v1, no filter support) leaves the ref blocked with the reason instead of crashing. Builds on [#79](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/79).
 - **`BootstrapLogger` now receives the bootstrap planning and progress lines.** They went only to the `-v` stderr log, so an embedder saw the GitHub size lookup and then nothing until the first checkpoint upload. A bootstrap that stalled while planning logged the size preflight and then nothing until its timeout. Every planning line now also goes to `BootstrapLogger`, with the logger's own attributes and the caller's context. Phase and checkpoint progress goes at Info: planning checkpoints, fetching the commit graph, planned remaining branches with their counts, push attempting, group pushed, branch finalized. A push the target refused or timed out, and resume markers left on the target, go at Warn; a push git-sync stops itself at its byte budget and then splits stays at Info, so a successful bootstrap logs no warnings. Lines logged once per branch (subsumed by trunk, already on target) go at Debug, so a repository with thousands of branches does not emit thousands of Info records per attempt. Error text from the target is sanitized. `-v` shows every line it showed before. ([#134](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/134))
 - **Batched bootstrap of a repository with thousands of branches now makes progress.** It used to fetch the commit graph of every branch, one request per branch, before it pushed anything. On a branch-heavy repository that planning alone outlasted a 30-minute sync budget, so each attempt timed out with nothing on the target and started again (ENT-3617). The trunk is now planned and pushed first, so an attempt that times out still leaves it on the target. The remaining branches share one commit-graph fetch. Small branches are pushed in shared packs that create their refs directly, so a fetch and a push deliver many of them. A group whose pack is over budget splits in half. A branch too big to share a pack, or one with a resume marker, keeps its own checkpointed batch as before. `FetchCommitParents` now takes the wants as a list of hashes.

@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+package gitproto
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/transport"
+)
+
+// MaximalFeature is entiredb's ls-refs extension. It is the capability
+// feature, the request argument, and the ref attribute. A server that
+// receives it marks each listed ref whose commit no other listed ref reaches.
+// It leaves a ref unmarked only when it has proved that another listed ref's
+// commit reaches it, so the marked refs imply the history of every listed ref.
+const MaximalFeature = "entire-maximal"
+
+// ErrMaximalUnsupported reports that a server does not advertise
+// MaximalFeature over protocol v2.
+var ErrMaximalUnsupported = errors.New("server does not advertise " + MaximalFeature)
+
+// ErrMaximalInconsistent reports a MaximalFeature listing that breaks the
+// server's own rules: a ref listed twice, two refs at the same object marked
+// differently, or a non-empty listing with no mark at all. Every non-empty set
+// of refs has a maximal one, so a listing like that cannot be trusted to drop
+// any have.
+var ErrMaximalInconsistent = errors.New("inconsistent " + MaximalFeature + " listing")
+
+// MaximalTips is a target's ls-refs listing with the MaximalFeature marks.
+// Reduce uses it to drop redundant haves.
+type MaximalTips struct {
+	marked   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
+	unmarked map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
+}
+
+// Marked and Unmarked report the listing's size, for logs and tests.
+func (m *MaximalTips) Marked() int   { return len(m.marked) }
+func (m *MaximalTips) Unmarked() int { return len(m.unmarked) }
+
+// ListMaximalTips lists conn's upload-pack refs under prefixes with the
+// MaximalFeature marks. It returns ErrMaximalUnsupported, before sending
+// ls-refs, when the server does not speak protocol v2 or, unless
+// assumeSupported is set, does not advertise the feature. Protocol v2 forbids
+// an argument the server did not advertise, so set assumeSupported only for a
+// server known to accept it; one that does not fails the ls-refs request.
+//
+// List only refs the source also holds. The source ignores a have it lacks,
+// and a marked tip it lacks hides the unmarked refs behind it, so the fetch
+// carries history the target already has. That costs bytes, never
+// correctness.
+func ListMaximalTips(ctx context.Context, conn Conn, prefixes []string, assumeSupported bool) (*MaximalTips, error) {
+	data, err := RequestInfoRefs(ctx, conn, transport.UploadPackService, GitProtocolV2)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	caps, err := DecodeV2Capabilities(bytes.NewReader(data))
+	if err != nil {
+		// A v1 advertisement: the server did not negotiate v2.
+		return nil, ErrMaximalUnsupported
+	}
+	if !caps.Supports("ls-refs") || (!assumeSupported && !caps.LSRefsSupports(MaximalFeature)) {
+		return nil, ErrMaximalUnsupported
+	}
+	args := []string{MaximalFeature}
+	for _, prefix := range prefixes {
+		args = append(args, "ref-prefix "+prefix)
+	}
+	body, err := EncodeCommand("ls-refs", caps.RequestCapabilities(), args)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	resp, err := PostRPC(ctx, conn, transport.UploadPackService, body, true, "upload-pack ls-refs "+MaximalFeature)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return decodeMaximalLSRefs(bytes.NewReader(resp))
+}
+
+func decodeMaximalLSRefs(r *bytes.Reader) (*MaximalTips, error) {
+	m := &MaximalTips{
+		marked:   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
+		unmarked: map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{},
+	}
+	// The server marks by peeled object, so every ref at one object carries
+	// the same mark.
+	markOf := map[plumbing.Hash]bool{}
+	reader := NewPacketReader(r)
+	for {
+		kind, payload, err := reader.ReadPacket()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		if kind == PacketFlush {
+			if len(m.unmarked) > 0 && len(m.marked) == 0 {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d refs, none marked", ErrMaximalInconsistent, len(m.unmarked))
+			}
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		if kind != PacketData {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected packet type %v in ls-refs response", kind)
+		}
+		fields := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(string(payload)))
+		if len(fields) < 2 {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs response line %q", payload)
+		}
+		name := plumbing.ReferenceName(fields[1])
+		// HEAD is not a have: the branch it names carries the same mark.
+		if fields[0] == "unborn" || name == plumbing.HEAD {
+			continue
+		}
+		if !plumbing.IsHash(fields[0]) {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("malformed ls-refs object id %q", fields[0])
+		}
+		hash := plumbing.NewHash(fields[0])
+		identity := hash
+		marked := false
+		for _, attr := range fields[2:] {
+			if attr == MaximalFeature {
+				marked = true
+			} else if peeled, ok := strings.CutPrefix(attr, "peeled:"); ok && plumbing.IsHash(peeled) {
+				identity = plumbing.NewHash(peeled)
+			}
+		}
+		if _, dup := m.marked[name]; dup {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
+		}
+		if _, dup := m.unmarked[name]; dup {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s listed twice", ErrMaximalInconsistent, name)
+		}
+		if prev, ok := markOf[identity]; ok && prev != marked {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: refs at %s marked differently", ErrMaximalInconsistent, identity)
+		}
+		markOf[identity] = marked
+		if marked {
+			m.marked[name] = hash
+		} else {
+			m.unmarked[name] = hash
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// Reduce returns haves without the refs the listing proved redundant. A nil
+// receiver returns haves unchanged. keep, when non-nil, names refs Reduce must
+// never drop, for a caller that filters those refs by rules of its own.
+//
+// An unmarked ref is implied only through a marked ref that reaches it, and
+// the listing does not say which one. So Reduce drops anything only when every
+// marked ref is in haves at its listed hash. A ref that moved since the
+// listing, such as one this run pushed, keeps the whole map unreduced. An
+// unmarked ref is dropped only at its listed hash. Refs the listing did not
+// cover stay.
+func (m *MaximalTips) Reduce(
+	haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
+	keep func(plumbing.ReferenceName) bool,
+) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
+	// No marks proves nothing; decodeMaximalLSRefs already rejects that
+	// listing, and this keeps a hand-built one from dropping every have.
+	if m == nil || len(m.unmarked) == 0 || len(m.marked) == 0 {
+		return haves
+	}
+	for name, hash := range m.marked {
+		if got, ok := haves[name]; !ok || got != hash {
+			return haves
+		}
+	}
+	out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash, len(haves))
+	for name, hash := range haves {
+		if listed, ok := m.unmarked[name]; ok && listed == hash && (keep == nil || !keep(name)) {
+			continue
+		}
+		out[name] = hash
+	}
+	return out
+}

index 00000000..90b6dcb5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/syncer/maximal.go
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+package syncer
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"log/slog"
+	"strings"
+
+	"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
+	"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
+)
+
+// fetchHaves returns the target refs a source fetch offers as haves:
+// targetRefs without the refs the target proved redundant (see
+// maximalTips), then narrowed by planner.FetchHaves.
+//
+// The reduction comes first because it needs every marked ref in the map. It
+// leaves independent-history refs to FetchHaves: an updated one may be
+// unmarked behind an unchanged one, and FetchHaves keeps the updated ref's old
+// value while dropping the unchanged one, so a reduction there would lose the
+// only have that shortens the update. A marked independent ref FetchHaves
+// drops reaches only its own namespace's history, so no other ref the
+// reduction drops depended on it.
+//
+// fetches says whether the caller will fetch a pack with these haves. The
+// listing costs round trips, so a run that fetches nothing (converged,
+// delete-only, or headed for a path that offers no haves) never asks for it.
+func (s *syncSession) fetchHaves(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
+	plans []planner.BranchPlan,
+	fetches bool,
+) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
+	if fetches && fetchesPack(plans) {
+		targetRefs = s.maximalTips(ctx).Reduce(targetRefs, s.independentHistoryRef)
+	}
+	return planner.FetchHaves(targetRefs, plans, s.cfg.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes)
+}
+
+func (s *syncSession) independentHistoryRef(name plumbing.ReferenceName) bool {
+	for _, prefix := range s.cfg.IndependentHistoryRefPrefixes {
+		if prefix = strings.TrimSpace(prefix); prefix != "" && strings.HasPrefix(name.String(), prefix) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// fetchesPack reports whether plans need objects from the source: a delete
+// moves no objects.
+func fetchesPack(plans []planner.BranchPlan) bool {
+	for _, plan := range plans {
+		if plan.Action == planner.ActionCreate || plan.Action == planner.ActionUpdate {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// maximalTips asks the target, once per run, which of its refs no other ref
+// reaches (gitproto.MaximalFeature). Every target tip is a have by default,
+// and most tips are ancestors of others, so a large target sends far more
+// have lines than the fetch needs.
+//
+// It returns nil, and the caller keeps every tip, when the target does not
+// advertise the feature (unless Config.AssumeTargetMaximal is set), when
+// protocol v1 is pinned, when the target has too few refs to gain anything,
+// when the target is reached over SSH, or when the listing fails or breaks the
+// server's own rules. An SSH server whose sshd does not accept GIT_PROTOCOL
+// answers the v2 probe with its full v0 ref advertisement, which can be
+// megabytes for a ref list this run already holds. HTTP and remote helpers
+// answer v2 with a short capability list. The listing is an optimization, so a
+// failure is logged and not returned.
+//
+// The listing runs on its own connection, never the push connection. With
+// FollowInfoRefsRedirect, upload-pack discovery may redirect to a read host,
+// and on a shared HTTPConn that redirect would carry the push and its
+// credentials there too.
+//
+// The listing covers only the namespaces this run mirrors. A marked target ref
+// the source lacks would hide the refs behind it from the fetch. Mirrored refs
+// came from the source, while a target-only namespace may not have.
+func (s *syncSession) maximalTips(ctx context.Context) *gitproto.MaximalTips {
+	t := s.target
+	if t == nil || t.conn == nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+	if t.maximalListed {
+		return t.maximal
+	}
+	t.maximalListed = true
+	if s.cfg.ProtocolMode == protocolModeV1 || len(t.refMap) < 2 || isSSHEndpoint(t.conn) {
+		return nil
+	}
+	probe, err := newConn(s.cfg.Target, "target", s.stats, s.cfg.HTTPClient)
+	if err != nil {
+		if s.logger != nil {
+			s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips unavailable; offering every target tip as a have", slog.Any("error", err))
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	defer probe.Close()
+	probe.SetProgressWriter(t.conn.ProgressWriter())
+	tips, err := gitproto.ListMaximalTips(ctx, probe, maximalRefPrefixes(planConfig(s.cfg)), s.cfg.AssumeTargetMaximal)
+	if err != nil {
+		if s.logger != nil && !errors.Is(err, gitproto.ErrMaximalUnsupported) {
+			s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips unavailable; offering every target tip as a have", slog.Any("error", err))
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	if s.logger != nil {
+		s.logger.Debug("target maximal tips", slog.Int("marked", tips.Marked()), slog.Int("unmarked", tips.Unmarked()))
+	}
+	t.maximal = tips
+	return tips
+}
+
+// maximalRefPrefixes is the target-side scope of the maximal listing: the
+// include prefixes when set, otherwise the namespaces the source listing uses.
+// A mapping keeps its kind (branch or tag), so the same prefixes cover its
+// target name. A ref outside the scope is unlisted, and Reduce keeps it.
+func maximalRefPrefixes(cfg planner.PlanConfig) []string {
+	var include []string
+	for _, p := range cfg.IncludeRefPrefixes {
+		if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
+			include = append(include, p)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(include) > 0 {
+		return include
+	}
+	return planner.RefPrefixes(cfg)
+}
+
+func isSSHEndpoint(conn gitproto.Conn) bool {
+	ep := conn.Endpoint()
+	return ep != nil && (ep.Scheme == "ssh" || ep.Scheme == "git+ssh")
+}

content.text:
**Verdict: no correctness bugs found at `ce8ba693`; one medium cost regression worth raising before merge.** Focused tests (`Maximal|Redirect|Credential` in `internal/gitproto` and `internal/syncer`) pass locally, and CI is green. Nothing is posted to the trail and no session is attached yet.

**Intent:** stop sending every target tip to the source as a have. The target (entiredb) marks the refs no other listed ref reaches, and git-sync drops the unmarked ones.

**Solution:** `ListMaximalTips` lists the target on a separate connection, once per run. `Reduce` drops unmarked refs only when every marked ref is still at its listed hash. A second commit holds credential-helper credentials to the site they were looked up for.

**What holds up**
- Fewer haves can only grow the pack, so the copy stays complete, including thin-pack bases.
- The relay check added in `executeIncremental` matches the one `incremental.Execute` makes, so the listing only runs when a pack is fetched.
- Every failure path (v1, SSH, unadvertised, rejected, inconsistent listing) falls back to offering every tip.
- The credential fix applies the same same-site rule explicit tokens already follow.

**Finding (medium, confidence ~0.8)** — `internal/gitproto/maximal.go`, `Reduce`
- **Trigger:** a marked target tip the source no longer holds, sitting on top of an unmarked ref. Examples are a branch deleted on the source and not pruned, or a force-pushed branch whose old tip the source has garbage-collected.
- **Impact:** the source ignores that have, and the refs behind it (for example `main`) were dropped. The pack then resends history back to the nearest marked tip the source does know, which can be the whole repository. Before this change `main`'s tip was a have and the pack was small. In sync mode without prune, this repeats every run and can hit pack size limits.
- **Evidence:** the trail's own `TestRun_IntegrationMaximalTipsTargetOnlyTipCostsBytesOnly` shows the fetch offering only the target-only tip. The changelog documents the cost but not that it is unbounded or recurring. I did not measure it on a large repository.
- **Suggested fix:** when a marked tip is not provably on the source (its hash is not in the source listing and it is not the old value of a planned non-force update), keep the unmarked refs whose hash the source advertises, or skip the reduction for that fetch.

**Not verified:** the credential fix beyond its tests, and behaviour against a real entiredb target.

```
target:   main → C      feature → X   (X's parent is C)
```

**Then on the source:** `feature` is rebased and force-pushed to `X'`, `main` advances to `D`, and the source garbage-collects `X`.

```
source:   main → D      feature → X'
target:   main → C      feature → X   (stale)
```

**Next sync run:**

1. The target's listing marks `feature` (nothing reaches `X`) and leaves `main` unmarked (`X` reaches `C`).
2. `Reduce` drops `main`, so the only have sent is `X`.
3. The source does not hold `X`, so it ignores the have. It now knows nothing the target has.
4. The source sends `D` and `X'` with their full history, which is the whole repository.

**Before this change:** the haves were `C` and `X`. The source ignored `X` but recognized `C`, and the pack held just the new commits.

**How long it lasts:**
- With a forced update or prune, the stale `X` is replaced in that run, so the cost is paid once per such rewrite.
- In sync mode without prune, a branch deleted on the source stays on the target as a marked tip, so every run that fetches pays it again.

The size depends on other branches: if the target has another marked tip the source still holds, the pack only goes back to that one. With `X` as the only tip above `main`, it is the full history.

content.text:
Yes, entiredb computes the marks, and in the example it computes them correctly: on the target, `X` really does reach `C`, so `feature` is maximal and `main` is not.

The problem is in what git-sync does with a correct answer. The marks say "these tips imply the rest **on the target**". git-sync then uses them to pick haves for the **source**, which only works if the source also holds every marked tip. entiredb cannot check that, because it knows nothing about what GitHub holds.

So the gap is in git-sync's `Reduce` (`internal/gitproto/maximal.go`) and its caller `fetchHaves` (`internal/syncer/maximal.go`). git-sync is the only place that sees both the target's marks and the source's ref listing, so the guard has to go there: when a marked tip is not known to be on the source, keep some unmarked refs the source does advertise.

The trail already acknowledges the assumption in a comment on `ListMaximalTips` ("List only refs the source also holds… costs bytes, never correctness"). My finding is that the cost can be the whole repository, and that a stale or force-pushed branch breaks the assumption even inside the mirrored namespaces.

Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away (under the manual
    checkpoint push policy it waits for 'entire checkpoint push'). The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.
